_comment: HOW A CHAIN'S TRACE YIELD IS MEASURED, fixed before a chain has a number to defend.
`tools/chain/lib/yield.mjs` reads this file; `tools/chain/yield-method-selftest.mjs` reads
it to check the module and the committed readings against it.
── WHY THE METHOD IS DATA AND WHY IT IS FIXED FIRST ────────────────────────────────────
A yield figure is the number that decides whether a chain ships, which makes it the
number most exposed to being chosen after the fact. Two ways of choosing it produce a
figure that looks fine:
* A SAMPLE OF TRANSACTIONS MEASURES THE SAMPLER. If the transactions inside a window
are chosen, the denominator becomes a function of what succeeded. Data-Contract.md
§5.2 already requires a snapshot to enumerate every transaction it saw INCLUDING the
ones it could not trace, each carrying a reason — so the honest denominator is
available for free and a chosen one has no excuse.
* A SINGLE AGGREGATE HIDES TWO WINDOWS MOVING IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. The per-window
figures over the observable population on the one chain measured here ranged from
50.5% to 100.0%. Reported only as the 78.4% total, neither end of that spread would
have existed, and the spread is the finding.
The method is therefore a file rather than a paragraph: a rule a new chain reads before
it measures cannot be adjusted by the chain that measured.
── THE IDS ARE `Y-` AND THEY ARE ASSERTED DISJOINT FROM TWO OTHER SETS ─────────────────
`snapshot-contract.json` carries the CONTRACT's rules (`S5-*`) and `health-checks.json`
the recording-health findings (`H-*`). This is a third kind of statement and must stay
one: the contract says what a producer must write, health says whether what it wrote is
worth publishing, and this says how a reading over it is COUNTED. The selftest requires
all three id sets to be pairwise disjoint, with an anti-vacuity guard on each side, for
the reason the health file gives: a rule stated twice is two answers to one question.
── THE CLASSIFICATION IS NOT RESTATED HERE ────────────────────────────────────────────
Which outcomes are traced, which are untraced and which mean the chain published no
execution at all is `snapshot-format.json`'s `outcomes`, read through
`lib/snapshot-format.mjs`'s `SNAPSHOT_OUTCOMES`. This file names EXCLUSIONS by the
population they remove and never by outcome token, and `lib/yield.mjs` imports the
partition rather than declaring one. A second classifier is a second place for the
denominator to drift, and `chain-health.mjs` already reads the same partition for its
own census.
── WHY A WINDOW IS AN ABSOLUTE RANGE AND NEVER A DEPTH ────────────────────────────────
MEASURED, not cautious. The five windows below were chosen against a tip of 76,024 on
blocks below tip. The tip was 87,073 on 2026-09-18. A re-run that picks windows "at the
same depths" therefore measures five windows about eleven thousand blocks away from the
ones the reading is over, and reports the difference as a change in the producer — which
is precisely the failure the pinning rule exists to prevent. A depth is a reading taken
against a moving tip; the reproducible identity is the range.
── WHAT A RE-RUN MAY AND MAY NOT MOVE, AND WHY THE COLUMNS ARE SPLIT ──────────────────
A re-run's columns are not all the same kind of claim. `chainColumns` are facts about
what the chain published and cannot move between two runs over the same absolute range.
`runColumns` are facts about this run's attempt and can. So a re-run whose CHAIN columns
are identical and whose RUN columns moved is a different event from one whose chain
columns moved, and the verdicts below keep them apart:
MEASURED 2026-09-18, and it is the case this split exists for. A re-run of the five
windows on the host that holds them reported 208 traced of 343, not 211. Three
transactions that replayed in the reading refused, all three named, all three with a
recorded observation beside them: the driver was spawned directly against a body proxy
and died with signal SIGSEGV after the VM had already simulated the transaction. That
host runs the WASM build of the VM because the prebuilt native addon will not execute
on its CPU. Every chain column was identical. So the reading is NOT reproduced — 208
is not 211 and the method must never say it is — and the producer is NOT broken, and
`differs-environmentally` is the verdict that says both. A method with only
`reproduced` and `not-reproduced` has to lie in one direction or the other.
── TWO PROPERTIES OF THE RECORD RATHER THAN OF THE CHAIN, CARRIED RATHER THAN FIXED ───
Both are under `carried` below, both are echoed by the module, and both bound what a
re-run can claim. The first is why `provenanceCoverage` is declared per chain and
checked: a reading whose windows do not all carry a replay ledger can assert "the same
windows reproduce" against recorded provenance for some of them and against nothing for
the rest, and the honest form is to say which.

_note: `windowsRequired` is a FLOOR on the number of windows a reading publishes, not a
ceiling. Five is what the chain measured here and what the method asks of a chain
whose history admits five; a chain whose replayable reach is a few days has fewer
distinct eras than windows and declares the shortfall under `pinned` rather than
padding the set with windows that differ by hours.

Y-WHOLE-WINDOWS.question: Is every transaction in each window counted, or only the ones that produced a trace?
Y-WHOLE-WINDOWS.healthy: Each window's `transactions` equals the enumerated row count for its absolute block range, and equals the sum of the populations the reading classifies those rows into.
Y-WHOLE-WINDOWS.fires: a window's `transactions` differs from the enumerated count, or from the sum of its populations
Y-WHOLE-WINDOWS.why: The failure this rule exists for is not arithmetic, it is that the denominator becomes the numerator. A count of rows that produced a trace, divided by itself, is 100% of a chain. The enumeration is the only quantity a run cannot influence, and §5.2 requires a producer to publish it, so the honest denominator is free.

Y-DENOMINATORS-NAMED.question: Does every published fraction say which population it is over, and is each excluded population named?
Y-DENOMINATORS-NAMED.healthy: The reading publishes one fraction per applied exclusion plus one over every transaction; each exclusion names the population it removes and its size; and each published percentage equals the one derived from those sizes.
Y-DENOMINATORS-NAMED.fires: a published percentage is not the derived one, an exclusion has no named population, or fewer than two fractions are published
Y-DENOMINATORS-NAMED.why: Two denominators is the FLOOR, not the count: a chain with more than one exclusion has more than two, and the chain measured here has three because it has two distinct exclusions. All of them are honest; quoting one without saying which is not. The equality with the derived figure is what stops a percentage being typed.

Y-ABSENT-IS-NOT-A-FAILURE.question: Is a transaction the chain never published as a public execution counted as a failure to trace?
Y-ABSENT-IS-NOT-A-FAILURE.healthy: Rows whose outcome is in the format's chain-absent population are removed by a NAMED exclusion and are not in the untraced count. Rows that carry a refusal reason ARE in it.
Y-ABSENT-IS-NOT-A-FAILURE.fires: a chain-absent row is counted as untraced, or an untraced row carrying a reason is excluded from the denominator
Y-ABSENT-IS-NOT-A-FAILURE.why: Trace-Artifacts.md §6's `absent` means the chain published no such execution — the chain's limit, not the producer's — so counting it as a failure understates every chain that has a private half and rewards a chain for having one. A refusal with a reason is the opposite case: it is ours, and dropping it from the denominator is the chosen denominator this method exists to forbid. The two look alike in a tally and are opposite in kind.

Y-PER-WINDOW-PUBLISHED.question: Are the per-window counts published beside the total?
Y-PER-WINDOW-PUBLISHED.healthy: Every pinned window has its own row, and the totals equal the sum of those rows column by column.
Y-PER-WINDOW-PUBLISHED.fires: a pinned window has no row, a row names an unpinned window, or a total is not the sum of its column
Y-PER-WINDOW-PUBLISHED.why: A total alone cannot show two windows moving in opposite directions, and a per-window arm is the only thing that can: two equal and opposite moves leave every total untouched. The rule is column-by-column rather than on the headline, because a headline built from a moved column and a compensating one is exactly the artefact being refused.

Y-WINDOWS-PINNED.question: Are the windows the ones this chain pinned, named by absolute range?
Y-WINDOWS-PINNED.healthy: The reading's window set equals the pinned set for its chain, exactly, as absolute ranges; and the reading's per-window recorded provenance matches the declared coverage.
Y-WINDOWS-PINNED.fires: a window is substituted, added or dropped; or the declared provenance coverage is not what the reading carries
Y-WINDOWS-PINNED.why: A window substituted for another invalidates the comparison, so a re-run over a different set is NON-COMPARABLE rather than a failed repeat — those are different findings and collapsing them turns a methodological error into an apparent regression. The provenance clause is here because a window with no replay ledger carries no runtime commit and no timestamp, so a claim that it reproduced rests on nothing; declaring the coverage is what stops the claim being made for the whole set.

Y-EXPECTED-VARIABLE.question: Did this chain state which variable it expected to dominate BEFORE it measured?
Y-EXPECTED-VARIABLE.healthy: The chain's entry declares exactly one `expectedDominantVariable` from the closed vocabulary, with the date it was declared and the reasoning.
Y-EXPECTED-VARIABLE.fires: no expectation is declared, or the declared variable is outside the vocabulary
Y-EXPECTED-VARIABLE.why: So the measurement can contradict the expectation instead of confirming a story written afterwards. It is also why no chain inherits another's answer: the one chain measured here found depth NOT MONOTONE — its third-deepest window beat its second-shallowest — while its two deepest windows were its two worst. That is a reading from five windows on one testnet. What generalises is the design; the answer about which variable dominated does not.

Y-BOUNDED-RANGE.question: Was the reading taken against a bounded historic range rather than against production traffic?
Y-BOUNDED-RANGE.healthy: Every window lies wholly inside the chain's declared `historicRange`, and every window's last block is below the finalized head recorded with the reading.
Y-BOUNDED-RANGE.fires: a window falls outside the declared range, or reaches the finalized head or beyond it
Y-BOUNDED-RANGE.why: A window that includes the tip is measuring live traffic: its transactions are still being served from a mempool, its bodies are warm, and a re-run over the same range a day later is a different set of transactions in the same block numbers. Recording the range is what makes the reading repeatable at all, and the finalized head is the mechanical boundary — above it the chain can still reorganise.

chainColumnsNote: WHAT `chainColumns` CLAIMS, AND THE TWO WAYS THE CLAIM IS NARROWER THAN IT READS.
Both were measured against this repository rather than imagined, and both are here
because the cost of the claim being wrong falls on the PRODUCER: a chain column that
moves for a reason outside the producer is reported `not-reproduced`, which is an
accusation, and it is the opposite failure from the one the split was built to avoid.
1. `privateOnly` — AND THEREFORE `withPublicHalf`, WHICH IS DERIVED FROM IT — IS NOT
A PURE CHAIN FACT. `ingest-range.mjs` files a row `private-only` when
`seen.publicCalls === 0`, and `publicCalls` is `tx.numberOfPublicCalls()` taken off
a body the off-chain file store served and `Tx.fromBuffer` decoded
(`lib/body-proxy.mjs`). So the column is a function of what that store served for
the hash and of which upstream decoder is installed, not only of what the chain
published. This is not hypothetical: before the `private-only` outcome existed,
every one of these 64 rows was `runtime-refused` off a driver `TypeError`, so the
column read 0 for the same chain over the same ranges — see
`migrate-refusal-reasons.mjs`, which exists to move them. `body-proxy.mjs` also
anticipates "a body written by a different serialisation" and files it
`truncated`, which moves the row to `bodyUnavailable` and moves `privateOnly` and
`withPublicHalf` with it. A producer or store upgrade therefore reads as
`not-reproduced` under this split, and that verdict blames the wrong thing.
2. NOTHING ANCHORS THE CHAIN'S IDENTITY. Comparability is decided by `sameWindows`,
which compares integer ranges and nothing else; neither artifact records a genesis
hash, a chain id, or a block hash at any window boundary. `Y-BOUNDED-RANGE` bounds
a REORG — every window below the finalized head recorded with that reading — and
says nothing about the two runs having seen the same history. A reset testnet, a
redeployed devnet or a node serving a different chain moves `transactions` over
the same block numbers, and the only verdict available for it is
`not-reproduced`. The honest verdict would be a second kind of `non-comparable`,
and adding one needs an identity field in the artifact rather than a rule here.
Three of the five columns — `transactions`, `firstInBlock`, `notFirstInBlock` — are
sound given the same history: they come off the block enumeration and are properties of
the block. The split is therefore kept, because the alternative is having no mechanical
separator at all, and these two limits are recorded so a chain reading them knows what
`not-reproduced` does and does not establish.

verdicts.non-comparable: the window sets differ, so the two readings are over different things. NOT a regression and not a repeat.
verdicts.reproduced: every column of every window is the baseline's.
verdicts.differs-environmentally: every chain column is the baseline's, some run column is not, and the attribution below reconciles — over the total AND inside every window. This is NOT `reproduced`: the figure is not the baseline's and may not be quoted as it.
verdicts.not-reproduced: anything else — a chain column moved, or a run column moved and the attribution does not reconcile.

requires: every differing transaction named by hash
its block named, and inside one of the pinned windows
a recorded observation, not an inference
the count of named transactions equal to the total movement in the traced column
and, in EVERY window, the largest absolute movement in any run column equal to the number of transactions named inside that window
_note: The fourth clause is what stops an attribution being a sentence. Three transactions
named against a movement of five is a partial explanation presented as a complete
one, and the arithmetic catches it without anyone reading the prose.
THE FIFTH CLAUSE WAS ADDED BECAUSE THE FOURTH ON ITS OWN WAS A FALSE GREEN, and it
was measured by planting it rather than reasoned about. `traced` is a SUM over
`tracedColumns`, so rows moving BETWEEN two of them — five `replayed` becoming five
`divergent` — leave `traced` untouched in that window and leave the total movement at
whatever the other windows contributed. Five unexplained divergences (a real
execution that DISAGREED with the block, the strongest signal this pipeline emits)
were accepted as `differs-environmentally` with the note "all attributed". It is the
same cancellation `Y-PER-WINDOW-PUBLISHED` refuses one level up, arriving between two
columns instead of between two windows.
It is a MAX and not a sum because one transaction leaving `replayed` for `refused`
moves three columns by one and is one transaction; and an EQUALITY and not a ceiling
because a transaction named in a window where nothing moved is an attribution to a
window that had none.
`bodyUnavailable` and `notAttempted` are in `runColumns` for the same reason: they
were in neither list, so a re-run in which the body store served forty fewer bodies
compared as identical. They are `declinedColumns` here and a re-run artifact is not a
reading, so `checkReading`'s own column sweep never sees one.

aztec-testnet.historicRangeRecordedBy: tools/chain/measurements/published-object-set.json, whose provenance records the contiguity walk over 1..75,971
expectationNotDeclaredBecause: THIS CHAIN CANNOT SATISFY `Y-EXPECTED-VARIABLE` AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT. It was
measured before the method was written down, so any expectation entered here now
would be a story written afterwards — which is the one thing that rule exists to
forbid. `Y-EXPECTED-VARIABLE` is therefore reported NOT MEASURED for this chain and
is never reported as passed, the same accounting `health-checks.json` uses for a
question its tool cannot yet answer.
It is also worth being exact about what this chain's five windows did and did not
establish, because the tempting summary is wrong in a way that would propagate. Over
the observable population the per-window figures were 50.5 / 71.4 / 100.0 / 95.7 /
100.0 %, shallowest last. So depth is NOT MONOTONE — the window 30,825 blocks down
at the time traced 100% while the one 7,825 down traced 95.7% — AND the two deepest
windows are markedly the two worst. Both halves are true and only the pair is
honest. "Depth is not the variable" drops the second half; "yield falls with depth"
drops the first. A chain arriving here with either as a prior would be inheriting a
conclusion drawn from five windows on one testnet, which is why the vocabulary is
declared per chain and checked per chain rather than defaulted.

exclusions.why: replaying transaction k needs the state left by the k before it, and no node method serves intra-block intermediate state — it exists only inside the sequencer. Permanent, and unrelated to age.

the execution has no public half at all: the private half ran in a wallet, was proved there, and only its effects were published. Permanent, and the chain's limit rather than the producer's — Trace-Artifacts.md §6's `absent`, published with no refusal reason and never counted as a failure to trace.

denominatorsNote: THREE, NOT TWO, and the count is a consequence of the exclusions rather than a
choice. `transactions` is everything the chain published; each further denominator
removes one named structural exclusion. The member column is the name the reading
publishes the population under and the yieldMember column is the name it publishes
the fraction under, so both directions are checkable: the member must equal
`transactions` minus the excluded populations, and the fraction must equal the one
derived from it. Neither is transcribed.

_note: The window with no replay ledger contributes 92 of the 211 traced — the largest
share of the total — and its `ledger` carries only `fetch`: no replay object, so
no runtime commit, no timestamp and no attempted/refused record. "The same five
windows reproduce the reading" is therefore assertable against recorded
provenance for FOUR of the five and against nothing for the fifth. That is not a
reason to drop the window — dropping it would be choosing windows by how well
they are documented — it is a reason not to quote its provenance as though it
existed.

carried.note: `ledger.replay.attempted` counts ONE PASS and is not a total. The replay loop opens by skipping any row already `replayed` or `divergent`, so a resumed pass attempts only what is still undecided — which, in a range whose successes are already recorded, is exactly the refused set. It therefore equals `refused` in every window that has a replay ledger, and the 45000-45199 window reads `attempted: 0` beside `replayed: 21`, which reads as a contradiction and is not one. THE CORPUS HOLDS BOTH PASSES OVER ONE WINDOW, which is why this is a measurement and not a caution: `historic-replay-yield.json` window 1-200 reads `attempted: 45` (resumed, equal to its refused) and `baseline-rerun.json` window 1-200 reads `attempted: 91` (a first pass into an empty state directory, equal to 43 replayed + 2 divergent + 46 refused). An auditor who quotes the field as "how many were tried" is wrong by the number already traced.
carried.bounds: nothing counted by this method may be taken from `attempted`; every published figure is counted from the rows

carried.note: See `provenanceCoverage` above. Four of five windows name runtime dfb9ebe23246...; the fifth names nothing. The figure it contributes is counted from rows and is not in doubt; what is absent is the record of the run that produced it.
carried.bounds: how widely a re-run may claim to have reproduced `the same windows`
